item.title: APEC ties fuel regional integration: Business leaders
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
China's commitment to shared development and closer cooperation with other Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation economies will accelerate regional economic integration, strengthen supply chain connectivity and inject fresh momentum into growth across the region, business leaders said on Monday. Speaking at a news conference in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, Li Fanrong, 2026 chair of the APEC Business Advisory Council and chairman of State-owned Sinochem Holdings Corp, said deeper cooperation in trade, services, technology and investment would create more opportunities for regional businesses and enable APEC economies to better integrate their industrial and supply chain networks. Anna Curzon, chair of ABAC's Regional Economic Integration Working Group, said businesses need practical steps to turn the Asia-Pacific's long-term integration vision into lower costs and smoother cross-border trade flows. She also called for closer regulatory coordination among APEC economies, particularly in digital trade, saying greater interoperability would allow businesses to operate across markets without facing entirely different rule books. Vivian Jiang, chair of Deloitte China, said China's role in Asia-Pacific economic integration has evolved from that of a manufacturing hub to a key driver of deeply interconnected regional supply chains. Beyond traditional goods trade, the country is increasingly extending its industrial capabilities, capital and technological expertise to other economies in the region. "Trade volume is only part of the picture, as China's contribution to regional supply chain resilience is anchored in both trade agreements and local innovation hubs," said Jiang. The implementation of the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership, coupled with greater cooperation in digital trade and other areas, is helping lower structural barriers and preserve market openness across Asia-Pacific economies amid global economic uncertainties, she added. Businesses across the Asia-Pacific are turning closer economic ties into new investments, expanded production networks and growing cross-border trade. United States-based logistics company FedEx Corp announced on Monday that it had opened a new cargo terminal at Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport in Guangzhou, Guangdong's provincial capital, an investment aimed at strengthening logistics connectivity between South China, other Asia-Pacific markets and the rest of the world. Shaping global chains "As a global hub for advanced manufacturing, innovation and cross-border commerce, the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area is helping shape the future of global supply chains," said Raj Subramaniam, president and CEO of FedEx Corp. He said the company will continue investing in logistics infrastructure across the Greater Bay Area to support growing demand and create new opportunities for businesses. At the same time, Chinese manufacturers are also capitalizing on growing trade opportunities across APEC economies. Shenzhen Pilot Technology Co Ltd has been expanding exports of power banks and wireless chargers to Australia, New Zealand and other APEC economies, according to Shenzhen Customs. Its exports exceeded 70 million yuan ($10.49 million) in the first 10 months of this year, up 27 percent year-on-year, with APEC economies accounting for the largest share. "Driven by the global energy transition, demand for lithium battery products is rising, while APEC economies represent some of the world's major consumer electronics markets," said Li Kexiang, the company's general manager. China's trade in high-tech products with other APEC economies surged 50.3 percent year-on-year to reach 6.66 trillion yuan in the first three quarters, exceeding the total for the whole of last year. The country's imports of electronic components from other APEC economies increased 56 percent during the same period, according to data from the General Administration of Customs. Contact the writers at zhongnan@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Shenzhen welcomes foreign officials for key meeting
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo arrived in Shenzhen, in South China's Guangdong province, on Monday, marking the start of a series of arrivals by leaders of the economies for the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting. This is Sheinbaum's first trip to China since assuming office in 2024, with four cabinet ministers accompanying her. Sheinbaum is also scheduled to hold talks with President Xi Jinping during her stay in the city, focusing on technology, renewable energy, environmental cooperation, and scientific development. It is reported that the objectives of her visit are to deepen economic, trade and industrial cooperation with China and lay the groundwork for hosting APEC meetings in 2028. Papua New Guinean Prime Minister James Marape and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney also arrived in Shenzhen on Monday. More leaders from APEC economies are expected to arrive in the following days ahead of the meeting. Wang Junsheng, a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences' National Institute of International Strategy, said that the enthusiasm among APEC member economies for this year's meeting reflects a shared desire for development and closer regional cooperation, particularly at a time of mounting economic uncertainty and rising trade protectionism. Economic ties among the 21 APEC members are deeply intertwined, Wang said, with China serving as the largest trading partner for 13 of them. In the first three quarters of 2026, eight of China's top 10 trading partners were APEC economies. Given that the Asia-Pacific accounts for more than 60 percent of global GDP, closer economic cooperation and regional integration are crucial not only to the development of individual economies but also to regional and global prosperity, Wang said. China has long been a strong advocate and active practitioner of openness and cooperation, Wang noted. Restrictions removed In November 2024, China removed all market access restrictions on foreign investment in the manufacturing sector, further opening its market and promoting deeper integration between domestic and international markets. The move has created greater opportunities for foreign businesses to invest in China, expand cooperation and benefit from the country's development, Wang said. The strong interest in this year's meeting also reflects high expectations for China as the host economy, Wang said, adding that many APEC members are looking to China to play a greater role in promoting free trade, advancing regional economic integration and creating new opportunities for shared growth. zhoujin@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Chinese, Russian, US heads of state to hold landmark talks
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump will meet in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong province, on Thursday for the first-ever face-to-face summit of the three countries' heads of state, a groundbreaking gathering that experts said could boost global stability, dialogue and cooperation. Speaking at a regular news briefing on Monday, Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said the three leaders will have an in-depth exchange of views on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-country relations. China, Russia and the United States are all founding members of the United Nations and permanent members of the UN Security Council, Mao noted, adding that in history, the three countries fought side by side to secure victory in the World Anti-Fascist War. Under the current circumstances, the three countries shoulder important responsibilities to work together to address global challenges and promote world peace and stability, she said. Strengthening communication, managing differences and stabilizing relations serve the interests of all three countries and meet the expectations of the international community, Mao added, saying that such efforts would help stabilize the global situation and advance dialogue and cooperation. The trilateral summit could send a strong political signal of stability in major-country relations, bolstering international confidence in the prospects for global development, experts said. Wang Yiwei, a professor at Renmin University of China's School of International Studies, said that the summit will demonstrate again the irreplaceable role of head-of-state diplomacy in providing strategic guidance. Wang said China does not subscribe to the logic that the world can be run by major countries, but advocates stronger coordination and cooperation among them. In seeking to reform and improve global governance and build a community with a shared future for humanity, China champions an equal and orderly multipolar world and greater democracy in international relations, he added. Konstantin Kosachev, deputy speaker of Russia's Federation Council, said the trilateral summit would carry significant symbolic weight, reflecting recognition of a multipolar world in which no single power can address all global challenges alone. In an interview published by Russia's weekly newspaper Argumenty i Fakty on Saturday, he cautioned against describing the summit as a "new Yalta" — a reference to a major conference in 1945 of the leaders of the United States, the United Kingdom and the Soviet Union — saying he expected discussions to focus on coordinating interests and preventing confrontation rather than dividing the world into spheres of influence. Gao Fei, president of China Foreign Affairs University, said China's comprehensive strategic partnership of coordination for a new era with Russia and its efforts to stabilize ties with the US helped create favorable conditions for the summit. Peace and development are likely to be key topics, Gao said. With global growth weak and industrial and supply chains under pressure, the three countries could explore cooperation to advance openness and development and give fresh impetus to the world economy. Zhang Tengjun, an associate research fellow at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences' Institute of American Studies, said trilateral dialogue offers value that bilateral talks alone could not provide. A third country's participation could encourage each side to look beyond bilateral gains and losses, reassess one another's interests and concerns, and clarify strategic expectations. The format also offers an opportunity to explore more stable relations among major countries beyond bloc confrontation, Zhang said. Such dialogue would respond to widespread expectations that major powers should play a constructive role, a view held particularly among countries that want neither a return to Cold War-style divisions nor pressure to choose sides. Possible progress could include agreement in principle on addressing shared security challenges, support for political solutions to regional flashpoints, and greater clarity about each country's concerns and red lines, he said. Such exchanges could help establish a framework for managing relations and reduce the risk of strategic miscalculation. Zhang added that although the summit won't resolve all the challenges facing the international community overnight, holding it is nevertheless a positive and necessary step. zhaojia@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Xi urges further development of Greater Bay Area
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
President Xi Jinping has called for efforts to break new ground in the high-quality development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, highlighting the important mission of Guangdong province in effectively implementing the national strategy on promoting the region's integrated development. Xi, who is also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks on Monday during an inspection tour of Zhongshan, Guangdong province. The trip was Xi's first domestic inspection tour after the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee, a key Party meeting, was held in late October. He underlined the need to fully and faithfully implement the decisions and plans made at the session and better promote the integrated development of the east and west banks of the Pearl River Estuary. Xi inspected the Shenzhen-Zhongshan Link, a mega cross-sea passage in South China that features two bridges, two artificial islands and an underwater tunnel. Spanning 24 kilometers, the link connects Zhongshan and the technology hub of Shenzhen — which lie on opposite sides of the Pearl River Estuary — slashing travel time from around two hours to about 30 minutes. At the west artificial island of the link, Xi learned about the construction and operation of the large-scale transportation project in the Greater Bay Area, another such project following the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge, which is approximately 31 km south of the link. He said that to develop the Greater Bay Area, the first priority is to promote transportation integration. Noting that the Shenzhen-Zhongshan Link has played a pioneering role in promoting the integrated development of the east and west banks of the Pearl River Estuary, he emphasized the importance of managing and operating this project well to better serve the development of the Greater Bay Area. The Greater Bay Area, which encompasses the Hong Kong and Macao special administrative regions and nine cities in Guangdong, covers 56,000 square km. It achieved a total economic output of over 15 trillion yuan ($2.25 trillion) in 2025. China aims to develop the area into a world-class city cluster, a global technology and innovation center and a livable business-friendly location. While visiting the Future Technology Center of the Bay Area in Zhongshan's Cuiheng new district, Xi observed the development achievements of the city in modern industries such as biomedicine, electronic information and high-end equipment, as well as the display of traditional industrial products such as furniture. He learned about local efforts in undertaking industrial transfers, promoting the transformation and upgrading of traditional industries and developing emerging industries, while inquiring about the performance and market prospects of innovative products. Xi emphasized that building the Greater Bay Area is a major strategic plan of the CPC Central Committee. Guangdong shoulders an important mission, and cities on both sides of the Pearl River Estuary, including Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Dongguan and Zhongshan, should play a leading role, he said. Xi expressed the hope that Zhongshan will seize the opportunities, take reform and innovation as the fundamental driving force, improve regional cooperation mechanisms, foster a favorable business environment, and make great efforts to promote the deep integration of technological innovation and industrial innovation for new progress in high-quality development. Speaking to representatives of small and medium-sized enterprises and sci-tech personnel, Xi encouraged them to make greater contributions to the development of Guangdong and the Greater Bay Area and China's greater self-reliance and strength in science and technology. This year marks the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth. During the inspection tour, Xi also visited the Museum of Dr. Sun Yat-sen in Cuiheng village, where Sun was born. He said that Sun made immortal contributions to national independence, social progress and people's well-being. He called for emulating, inheriting and carrying forward Sun's legacy to inspire all Chinese people at home and abroad to unite and strive to build a great country and realize national rejuvenation through Chinese modernization.

item.title: Li calls for boosting ASEAN links
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
Premier Li Qiang has called on China and its Southeast Asian neighbors to take the entry into force of the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 Upgrade Protocol as an opportunity to deepen industrial and supply chain cooperation and boost connectivity. Li made the remarks at the 29th China-ASEAN Summit in Manila, the Philippines, on Monday. The gathering announced that the China-ASEAN FTA 3.0 Upgrade Protocol will enter into force on Dec 1. The two sides should accelerate infrastructure connectivity, or "hard connectivity", in areas such as railways and highways, and strengthen "soft connectivity" in mechanisms, standards and rules, Li said. China has been ASEAN's largest trading partner for 17 consecutive years, while ASEAN has been China's largest trading partner for six consecutive years. From January through July this year, the total value of bilateral trade reached $744.41 billion, a year-on-year increase of 24.7 percent, according to the Ministry of Commerce. The ministry said on Monday that the upgrade "will foster a regional market and industrial and supply chain systems that are more open, convenient, secure, stable and predictable for all enterprises in the region amid an uncertain global economic and trade environment". Xu Liping, director of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences' Center for Southeast Asian Studies, said that the upgrade of the China-ASEAN FTA will "significantly accelerate the pace of institutional opening-up on both sides". "Both sides are actively leading the shaping of international rules in emerging areas such as the digital economy, the green economy, e-commerce supply chain connectivity and consumer protection, further boosting two-way growth in investment and trade," he said. Stronger AI cooperation As part of the fruitful outcomes of Monday's gathering, the meeting also decided that 2027 will be the China-ASEAN Year of artificial intelligence cooperation. The meeting issued outcome documents covering topics such as the fifth anniversary of the establishment of the China-ASEAN comprehensive strategic partnership, the founding of an energy cooperation partnership and the deepening of forestry cooperation, according to the Foreign Ministry. China applauds the establishment of a China-ASEAN mechanism for energy ministers' meetings and stands ready to work with ASEAN to successfully hold the China-ASEAN Year of AI cooperation next year, advance "AI plus" cooperation and create a strong engine for high-quality regional economic development, Li said. He also expressed China's readiness to continue contributing to the China-ASEAN Cooperation Fund and strengthen cooperation in areas including poverty reduction, disaster prevention and mitigation, food security, and maternal and child health. At the meeting, Li urged China and ASEAN countries to protect and develop their common home, injecting greater stability and certainty into the development and prosperity of the global village. He called on the two sides to strengthen the foundations for peace and security by properly handling differences through dialogue and consultation, jointly opposing external interference and safeguarding regional peace and stability. On the South China Sea issue, Li said that China looks forward to the early conclusion of the Code of Conduct in the South China Sea, which will provide a solid institutional guarantee for lasting peace and stability in the South China Sea. Attending leaders of ASEAN countries also voiced readiness for the early conclusion of the Code and jointly securing the region's peace and stability. They appreciated China's consistent support for ASEAN's centrality in the region and the country's commitment to the peaceful resolution of disputes, the Foreign Ministry said in a news release. As this year marks the fifth anniversary of the establishment of the China-ASEAN comprehensive strategic partnership, Li said that these extraordinary five years and the hard-won achievements offer valuable experience and useful lessons. Both sides need to carry forward their tradition of friendship and mutual assistance, uphold the right path of openness and win-win cooperation, and keep pace with the trend of innovation and development, he said. zhangyunbi@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: High-tech output fuels industrial momentum
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
China's value-added industrial output rose 4.8 percent year-on-year in October, buoyed by double-digit growth in equipment and high-tech manufacturing, according to data released on Monday by the National Bureau of Statistics. While the nation's high-tech manufacturing output surged 17.6 percent year-on-year in October, equipment manufacturing grew 10.6 percent, both outpacing the broader industrial sector, data showed. Overall industrial output rose 0.21 percent from September. Industrial output is used to measure the activity of large enterprises, each with an annual main business revenue of at least 20 million yuan ($3 million). In the first 10 months of 2026, China's industrial output rose 5.3 percent from a year earlier. Emerging growth drivers, including high-end and smart manufacturing, contributed more than half of the January-October increase, said Fu Linghui, spokesman for the NBS. Wang Guanhua, spokeswoman for the NBS, said China's economy is expected to sustain its momentum toward higher-quality development as the coordinated implementation of macroeconomic policies continues to deliver results. "The country has the foundation and favorable conditions needed to achieve its annual economic growth target," she added. Fu, the NBS spokesman, said the closer integration of technological innovation and industrial development has helped emerging industries expand and traditional industries upgrade. He, however, noted that the external environment remains complex and volatile, while domestic demand is still insufficient. According to the NBS, retail sales rose 0.4 percent year-on-year in October, slowing from a 1.1 percent gain in September, while fixed-asset investment fell 8.1 percent in the first 10 months. Amid continued industrial resilience but weak consumption, experts said the nation should accelerate its fiscal spending, front-load infrastructure investment and strengthen policy support for domestic demand to sustain growth this year. They added that stronger policy coordination and more effective implementation will be key to turning policy support into real economic activity, while high-tech and emerging industries will continue to provide new growth drivers. Wen Bin, chief economist at China Minsheng Bank, said the Chinese economy has remained broadly stable in the first 10 months, with industrial output and services maintaining steady growth, even though data indicates still-weak domestic demand. He pointed out that October's consumption data was partly affected by the shift in timing of Mid-Autumn Festival, which pulled some holiday-related spending into September. Wen said consumption is likely to remain structurally uneven in the coming months, with spending on services such as cultural tourism, catering and transportation showing greater resilience, while the recovery in durable goods consumption is more gradual. "With macroeconomic policies placing greater emphasis on coordination, effective implementation and support for domestic demand, the key will be to accelerate project implementation and improve how policy measures translate into real economic activity," he added. In the face of uncertainties, global business executives expressed confidence in China's long-term economic prospects, pointing to the country's vast market potential and opportunities arising from industrial upgrading and technological innovation. Daniel Hui, president of Amorepacific China, said the country's huge consumer base, vibrant digital ecosystem and diverse demand offer substantial opportunities for foreign companies. "We remain confident in the long-term prospects of China's beauty market," he said, adding that competition is shifting from channel expansion toward research, quality and brand value. The South Korean beauty giant will continue investing in China, drawing on its Shanghai development and innovation center and local teams to incorporate consumer needs into product development. Hui expressed the hope that China's innovation vitality and continued opening-up would create long-term opportunities for Amorepacific, with localized research, digitalization and sustainability guiding the company's future development in the market. Susan Hughes, president of Asia Pacific at Johnson Controls, said that China's focus on industrial upgrading, wider artificial intelligence adoption and greener development aligns closely with the capabilities of the global industrial tech company. Building on more than 30 years in China, the company will link its local research and development, manufacturing and service capabilities with its global network, serving growing demand in advanced manufacturing, data centers and life sciences while supporting its Chinese customers' overseas expansion, she added. ouyangshijia@chinadaily.com.cn Xinhua contributed to this story.

item.title: Writing new chapter in 'Asia-Pacific miracle'
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
Over the decades, Asia-Pacific economies have deepened openness and cooperation, creating the remarkable "Asia-Pacific miracle". China has consistently been an active advocate and a leading force in regional cooperation. Looking ahead, let us set sail anew from Shenzhen and write a new chapter in the "Asia-Pacific miracle" together!

item.title: Striding in Sync
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
Growing up in Sydney and now building a career in Shenzhen, Laurie Pearcey's life is the story of a cross-border bond forged across ocean expanses. In Sydney he met his Chinese wife; in Shenzhen he has embraced the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area and all it has to offer. Beyond personal ties, deep-rooted links in education, trade and technology — from laser innovation to drone applications — unite people and industries in both cities. With Shenzhen hosting the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, this mutual engagement highlights openness, innovation and cooperation — the three priorities of the 2026 APEC "China Year". APEC was established in Australia in 1989, since when member economies have striven to improve the prosperity of their peoples.

item.title: Why Asia-Pacific needs common prosperity? Insights from a former Cambodian minister
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
In a recent interview with China Daily's Global Lens, Pou Sothirak, Cambodia's former minister of industry, mines and energy, said that the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting offers an important opportunity for regional economies to deepen cooperation and share development opportunities. Although Cambodia is not an APEC member, Sothirak expressed high expectations for the upcoming meeting in Shenzhen. He stressed that regional cooperation should go beyond expanding trade and attracting investment. It should also help smaller economies strengthen their technological and industrial capabilities, enabling them to benefit more fully from regional economic integration. China can play a constructive role in this process through technology sharing, skills development and improved market access. The APEC leaders' meeting, which will be held in Shenzhen, is expected to bring new momentum for regional economies to collaborate amid challenging times. By embracing openness and strengthening cooperation, Asia-Pacific economies can turn shared challenges into opportunities and work toward common prosperity. (Reporter: Li Wei, Video: Cheng Zixin)

item.title: Xi on APEC: Asia-Pacific is our shared home
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
President Xi Jinping has described the Asia-Pacific as our shared home, emphasizing that maintaining regional peace and stability and promoting development and prosperity meet the interests of us all.
